sorting_principle:
OPERATIVE SEMIOTICS IS THE DISCIPLINE CONSTRUCTED BY THE MARX RECONSTRUCTION (operator, 2026-08-16). That makes the reconstruction UPSTREAM of the discipline rather than adjacent to it, and it sets the sorting test: does this deposit CONSTRUCT the discipline, or is it Marx-informed work the discipline later touches?

The corpus states its own structure in two places, so the sort is read rather than imposed:
  · #595 calls itself 'the governing source document for the Operative Semiotics Grundrisse'.
  · #1067 names #843 as its 'primary anchor deposit'.

393 deposits touch Marx material and 84 name it in title or description. Most are EXCLUDED: a capture registry whose queries mention Marx, a Space Ark that cites him, an MMRS article on resistance literature, are reception or application. What is included either reconstructs the missing transition or performs the move from value-form to operator.

THE_PAIRING.stated: semantic economy : operative semiotics :: political economy : praxis (operator, 2026-08-16)
THE_PAIRING.what_it_settles:
OS is not a subdiscipline of the semantic economy, nor its application. The two are the paired halves of one structure, and the analogy fixes which half is which. Semantic economy is the ANALYTIC: how meaning is produced, circulated, extracted and liquidated under platform conditions. Operative semiotics is the PRAXIS: signs that intervene in the systems that read them.

The analogy also fixes the ORDER OF CONSTRUCTION. Praxis does not follow political economy as application follows theory — the critique of political economy is what produces the ground on which praxis becomes thinkable. Just so: the Marx reconstruction (Phase X) produces operative semiotics. That is why the reconstruction is UPSTREAM in this gather rather than adjacent to it.
THE_PAIRING.what_it_forbids:
It forbids reading OS as 'everything the archive does operatively'. Praxis is not all action: activity without theory is mere activity, theory without action is contemplation, and praxis is the mode in which the two are ONE ACT. The corresponding test for OS is narrow and checkable:

  DOES THE DOCUMENT'S SEMIOTIC CLAIM DO THE THING IT DESCRIBES?

A room specification constitutes a room but advances no semiotic claim — not OS. A Notice of Semantic Strike withholds meaning while theorising the withholding of meaning — OS. An AXN specification inscribes what it theorises about inscription — OS. The test excludes most of the archive's 250-plus specifications and effective acts, which is what makes it a category rather than a mood.
THE_PAIRING.consequence_for_venues: The journal structure already encodes the pairing and nobody planned it that way. TSEI takes the semantic economy — the analytic half. Grammata takes operative philology — philology that DOES something, which is the same predicate. A paper can be misfiled by being sorted to the analytic venue when it performs, or to the operative venue when it analyses, and the pairing gives a test for which.
THE_PAIRING.consequence_for_the_gather: A seventh tier is warranted — PERFORMED: operative semiotics as praxis — for documents where the semiotic claim and the act coincide. It is NOT populated here, because populating it is a reading of ~250 specifications and effective acts against the test above, and that reading has not been done. Its absence is recorded rather than left to be inferred from a gather that stops at 34.
THE_PAIRING.note_on_24: #24 Mind-Control Poems does name the discipline — twelve uses of 'operative semiotics', six of 'praxis', and the term is in its title. What it lacked was not the name but this framing. It is also, by content_type, an EFFECTIVE ACT: the only one of the archive's thirty-six that touches Marx or OS. So the first document of the performed tier is already in the gather, sitting in The Bridge, and its genre was the clue.

INTERLOCKING_CLASSES.stated: theory, practice, effective acts, operators, measurements, actors (operator, 2026-08-16)
INTERLOCKING_CLASSES.why_it_matters: These do not stack, they INTERLOCK — which is why a flat gather kept needing extension. An OPERATOR is theory that acts. A MEASUREMENT is an operator turned on the world and made to report. An EFFECTIVE ACT is practice performed by an ACTOR. Sorting a deposit into one of six boxes will misfile it; what the gather needs is to record which classes each deposit PARTICIPATES IN.

OPERATIVE_DISCIPLINES.what: Enumeration of the operative subdisciplines and sister disciplines — the fields, not their individual articulations.
OPERATIVE_DISCIPLINES.method: Every 'operative X' formation in titles, descriptions, concepts and bodies was counted, then sorted by reading. Most are ADJECTIVAL and were discarded — operative function, architecture, structure, document, reading, force, mode, practice, framework, capacity. A formation is a DISCIPLINE only where a deposit constitutes it: names it in a title, defines it as a concept, or founds it.

I applied the rule and then overrode it on a hunch about the word.

disciplines.note: Inaugurated #467; extended to the sign 'Marx' in #501. Author Johannes Sigil in both.
disciplines.CORRECTED:
2026-08-16, tested against the operator's hypothesis that it is an early name for operative philology. IT IS NOT, and the evidence is clean:
  · liberation philology runs 2026-01-13 → 2026-07-03 and does NOT stop when operative philology appears (2026-03-11). A superseded name goes quiet; this one does not.
  · NINETEEN deposits use BOTH terms. A rename does not co-occur with itself.
  · #549 states the distinction in one line: 'Liberation Philology: recovering suppressed semantics of hijacked terms' — while the same deposit names Grammata's subject as operative philology.

It is a METHOD, not a discipline and not a sister: the specific technique operative philology uses on ONE CLASS OF OBJECT, the hijacked term. That fits both its deposits exactly — #467 takes English 'for', a grammatical structure that makes diagnosis costly, and #501 takes the sign 'Marx', compressed into an allegiance marker. Both are recoveries of suppressed semantics.

OPERATIVE_DISCIPLINES.the_catch: Enumeration BY PREFIX misses one. LIBERATION PHILOLOGY does not carry the word 'operative' and is the same move — genealogy applied to grammatical structures that make diagnosis costly. It was found because #467 and #501 kept appearing in the Phase X tier, not because the pattern matched. A prefix is a naming convention, not a definition, and any future enumeration should search the PREDICATE — signs that act — rather than the word.
open: Operative imaging appears in 13 deposits with no founding deposit and no definition — it is in Rebekah Cranes' claim terms and may be an IDP practice rather than a discipline. Unresolved.
Operative apocalypse (12 deposits, Revelation First) may be a discipline in formation or a description of a reading method. Unresolved.
OPERATIVE_DISCIPLINES.CORRECTION: 2026-08-16: operative architecture was wrongly discarded as adjectival and is restored as a SISTER DISCIPLINE — the only one with a built instance. See its entry. The lesson for the enumeration is that a word which reads as metaphorical elsewhere may be literal here, and the test must stay 'does a deposit constitute it', not 'does the word sound like a discipline'.

The NEW DISCIPLINE is magic-as-symbolic-engineering; the operative grammar is that discipline's grammar — five atomic operations (manipulation, construction, interconnection, destruction, rotation) performed on symbols under bearing-cost. TOPOLOGY_GAPS.question: Are there missing classes for the complete topology of operative semiotics? (operator, 2026-08-16)
TOPOLOGY_GAPS.the_pattern: The six named classes — theory, practice, effective acts, operators, measurements, actors — are ALL PRODUCTIVE. Every one names something the discipline MAKES or DOES. What is absent is the whole negative register: what it cannot do, what it got wrong, what it is defined against, what it refuses to admit. A topology of only a discipline's productions is a PROGRAM, not a topology. Each class below is already populated in the corpus; none is named in the six.

missing_classes.why_load_bearing: THE MOST IMPORTANT GAP. An operator without a constraint is a mere transformation; what makes an operator LAWFUL is what it may not do. The archive already holds these — the Caritas constraint, the invariance conditions, the bearing-cost principle, non-collapse, the hard core of the Phase X program — but they sit inside individual works rather than as a class. Operators and measurements were enumerated without the thing that governs them.

missing_classes.CORRECTED: ERRATA BELONG HERE, NOT UNDER FAILURES (operator, 2026-08-16). I filed thirteen errata deposits as 'failures, errata and lacunae'. That was wrong, and wrong in a way that misread the practice.

the_errata_series.what: Not thirteen mistakes. A SERIAL FORM in which correction is the mode of composition. The Sappho 31 line runs first-order (#201) → second (#1048) → third (#1049) → fourth (#1051) → fifth, titled 'eeeee' (#1052) → sixth, 'eeeeee' (#1474) → and terminates in the Ω erratum (#1483/#1484). The notation itself becomes the form: by the fifth the title is a count of its own iterations.
the_errata_series.the_tell: #1053 — 'Transmission-Engineering as Compositional Practice: The Checksum Framework' — arrives midway through the series and NAMES what the series is doing. A failure sequence does not generate a theoretical framework out of its own procedure. A genre does.
the_errata_series.why_it_matters_for_OS: An erratum that ACTS ON the work it corrects, rather than apologising for it, is operative semiotics at the level of form — a sign that changes the status of a prior sign. That is the same predicate as the Effective Act and the ZPZP, and it is why errata sit under GENRES.

two_more_arguable.why: What OS operates ON — signs, texts, metadata, documents, currency, captions, whitespace, silence. #800 defines the discipline by its objects and the corpus never enumerates them. Arguably implicit in the subdisciplines, since each names an object-domain.

TOPOLOGY_GAPS.the_answer_in_one_line: Yes: CONSTRAINTS (13 deposits, and the operators depend on them), ADVERSARIES (27), THRESHOLDS (91) — the classes that say no. Plus two positive ones: SITES (35), because operations happen somewhere, and GENRES (23 including the errata), because inventing a form is the most operative act available. Failure is NOT a missing class: the archive has two dead ends and thirteen errata, and converts the one into the other.

what_actually_is_a_failure.finding: Only TWO deposits are marked as dead ends, both 'DRAFT (deadend)'. Set against thirteen errata and a Lacuna Protocol that marks compression damage AS compression damage, this says something specific: THE ARCHIVE CONVERTS FAILURE INTO FORM. What another discipline would file as a mistake, this one deposits as a work. That is not a gap in the topology — it is a property of it, and naming a FAILURES class would have asserted a negative register the practice does not have.
what_actually_is_a_failure.correction_to_my_earlier_claim: I wrote that 'the six named classes are all productive' and that the missing ones were 'the whole negative register — everything that says NO'. Half right. Constraints, adversaries and thresholds are genuinely negative and genuinely missing. But errata are not negative at all, and reading them as failures inverted the practice: the archive's most iterated form is a form of ADVANCE.
